appraisal_events.evidence: il vous aime beaucoup, tout le monde vous aime beaucoup... C'est un homme d'une grande valeur, qui sait énormément... j'en suis moi-même étonné. — narrator's aside: qui ne se doutait sans doute pas... qu'en son absence, il ne se gênait pas pour dauber sur lui.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus praises Brichot as unusually broad-minded and valuable, unaware — as the narrator immediately notes — that Brichot mocks him behind his back and is already helping engineer his downfall.

appraisal_events.evidence: un pauvre Swann aveuglé par la jalousie et par l'amour, tels ces hommes dont pas un seul n'avait été deviné par lui... il m'aurait tué tout simplement, il était jaloux comme un tigre... c'est elle qui lui a tiré des coups de revolver que j'ai failli recevoir.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus's condescending reminiscence recasts Swann as a blind, tormented jealous lover, manipulated by Odette and by Charlus himself without ever suspecting the truth, deflating Swann's reputation for perceptiveness.

appraisal_events.evidence: Brichot tirait parfois de cette présence de M. de Charlus à ses cours l'occasion de faire un plaisir... le baron de Charlus, prince d'Agrigente, le descendant des Condé, assistera à mon cours. C'est un souvenir à garder que d'avoir vu un des derniers descendants de notre aristocratie qui ait du type.
appraisal_events.explanation: Brichot trades on Charlus's aristocratic pedigree to do favors for bourgeois acquaintances, dangling his presence as a rare spectacle worth attending a lecture for.

status_effects.explanation: Charlus, the most demanding judge present, rates Brichot's mind and manner unusually highly, a real if undeserved elevation in his eyes.
The narrator's aside reveals Charlus's warm trust in Brichot to be dangerously misplaced, since Brichot secretly disparages him and is complicit in the plot forming against him.
Retold through Charlus's condescending anecdotes, Swann appears as a jealous, thoroughly deceived figure, oblivious to Charlus's own prior claim on Odette and to the affairs unfolding around him.
Charlus positions himself as the definitive authority on Swann's private history ('je connais ça comme personne'), a display of superior insider knowledge and narrative control.
He gains social currency among bourgeois families by offering a glimpse of a genuine aristocrat at his lectures, trading on Charlus's name to enhance his own standing as host of a rare access.
Charlus is treated less as a person than as a curiosity to be gawked at — a young woman studies him as a 'descendant de Condé' surprised he doesn't wear a ruff — reducing him to a relic on display.

ambiguities: Charlus's account of his own prior claim on Odette and his central role in the Swann-Odette history is delivered by a notoriously self-mythologizing speaker, so the diminishment of Swann in E2 should be read as Charlus's flattering-to-himself version of events rather than a fully neutral narratorial verdict.
